The issue at hand within the Sanders camp is election fraud, not voter fraud. The reports are that voters party affiliations were switched without them doing so, not that people who shouldn't be voting were. Happened to Trump as well, but he doesn't need to make those waves having won in Arizona.

The real problem is that people forget the difference between voter fraud and election fraud. Voter fraud (pretending to be someone else at the polls) is such a stupidly inefficient way to try and rig an election that no one even bothers to attempt it. Election fraud (rigging the election system to get the vote results you want) is much more effective and is actually carried out by elected officials. Things like voter suppression are sort of a grey area that don't technically fall under election fraud, but are still used to effect the outcome of a vote.

An example of voter fraud is standing in line to vote and giving your neighbors name when asking for a ballot. An example of election fraud would be rigging it (in an illegal way) so you're guaranteed to have your candidate's name first on the ballot (giving them a bump in votes). Voter suppression would be something like voter ID laws, or requiring voters register an inordinate amount of time ahead of the election.
